outline.description: This chapter establishes the context of the dispute, detailing the relationships between the insureds, the insurer, and the premium finance company, as well as the procedural history leading to the appeal.
subtopics: Identification of Plaintiffs (Williams, Wright, Jenkins) and Defendants (GoAuto, APAC)
The Premium Finance Arrangement: Installment payments and Power of Attorney
The Triggering Event: Default on payments and subsequent policy cancellations
Litigation History: Class action filing, removal to federal court, and summary judgment
Procedural Posture: Appeal from the District Court's dismissal with prejudice

outline.chapter_title: The Louisiana Statutory Framework for Policy Cancellation
outline.description: This chapter outlines the specific Louisiana statute governing premium finance cancellations and the judicial doctrines surrounding its application, which form the basis of the legal analysis.
subtopics: Overview of La. Rev. Stat. § 9:3550(G)(3)(a)–(b)
Statutory Requirements: Notice, certification, and delivery methods
The Strict Adherence Doctrine: Mandate for exact compliance (*Delatte*, *Eaglin*)
Legislative Purpose: Fixing cancellation time and granting cure periods (*Britten*)
Consequences of Non-Compliance: Ineffective cancellation and liability

outline.chapter_title: Statutory Interpretation: The Certification and Signature Requirement
outline.description: This chapter analyzes the Plaintiffs' first argument regarding whether the statutory requirement to 'certify' information necessitates a physical signature on the cancellation notice.
subtopics: Plaintiffs' Argument: Implicit signature requirement for certification
Statutory Textual Analysis: Absence of explicit signature mandate in § 9:3550
Review of Louisiana Case Law: Lack of direct precedent on signatures
Distinguishing *Benitez v. Elsayed*: Absence of certification vs. absence of signature
Court's Conclusion: 'Certifying' does not require a named employee signature

outline.chapter_title: Statutory Interpretation: The Requirement of Receipt
outline.description: This chapter examines the second compliance argument concerning whether the insurer must physically possess the cancellation request before effecting cancellation, specifically addressing electronic transmission.
subtopics: Plaintiffs' Argument: 'Receipt' requires physical possession by a GoAuto employee
Definition of 'Receipt': Black's Law Dictionary analysis
Electronic Systems: Web services and automated possession as valid receipt
Timeline of Cancellation: Automatic system cancellation vs. later physical stamping
District Court's Alternative Ruling: Rejection of the 'private carrier' theory

outline.description: This chapter covers the Plaintiffs' procedural request to certify questions to the Louisiana Supreme Court and the Fifth Circuit's final ruling on the appeal.
subtopics: Request for Certification: Plaintiffs' argument for state court interpretation
Standard for Certification: *Jefferson v. Lead Indus. Ass'n* and 'compelling reason' threshold
Court's Reasoning for Denial: Lack of necessity and preservation of certification resource
Final Holding: Affirmance of the District Court's summary judgment
Significance: Validation of automated cancellation procedures under Louisiana law
